chapter: Second interview: bass, Parker and Miles
title: Birdland night with Bird, Bud Powell and Art Blakey; God and no God
summary: Johnson recalls the collapsed set; Mingus remembers a photo of Bud in Bird's arms and a conversation about God.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Charlie Parker: encounters, lore and legacy

blocks.x: Yeah. I remember that night at Birdland. You were in the band and Max and Bud Powell and I think Kenny Durham. And there was that awful business with -- he started yelling for Bud to get on the stand.
That wasn't Max. That was Art Blakey.
Art Blakey, right, yeah. And I remember, you were trying to bring some sanity to the whole thing, but finally --
I thought I was. I shouldn't have said nothing.
Why?
Not as crazy as he was.

Well, he seemed so that night. But did he seem a tragic figure to you? At times? Because, I remember one night, I was coming downstairs and as I said, I barely knew him. But he was going upstairs, tears going down his eyes, and he said, I've got to see you, I've got to see you tomorrow. And he looked so sad.
There's a picture of him and Bud Powell that night, and -- have you seen that way, where Bud was laying in ______ arms?
No.
And Bud looks like a puppet. I don't know where that picture -- this is (inaudible). They both

look like they're out. Bud looked like he was a puppet, laying in Bird's arms. That night, Bird was talking, deep conversation, we were talking about philosophy, we were talking about God and no God. And the time to go to work, he said, well, maybe we can discuss it on the bandstand.
And that was the set where it all collapsed, huh?
Might have been.
Yeah. Where was he in the God-no-God situation?
Well, if there was none, he was.
In other words, if there was no God, man was God.
No, he was.
Oh, why he?

We was talking, and said there's no God, and he says, well, (inaudible) I'll take it. Says, if you don't believe in God, then I'll take the job. That was out at Accoustics. That was some years before that.
So that would seem to indicate that he himself did believe in something.
Yeah, he believed in God.
